title: Fix a leaky sink supply fitting
summary: Stop a drip at the compression nut where the sink supply line meets the shutoff valve. HAND-WRITTEN FIXTURE for Parts 2/3 development; not produced by the pipeline.

safety.text: Do not over-tighten: a cracked ferrule or valve body leaks worse.

objects.name: shutoff valve
objects.visual_description: Small chrome valve on the wall under the sink with an oval or round handle, supply line coming out of the top.

objects.name: compression nut
objects.visual_description: Hex nut on the valve outlet where the braided supply line attaches.

objects.name: bucket
objects.visual_description: Any small bucket or a folded towel.

steps.title: Turn off the water
steps.tooltip: Turn the shutoff valve clockwise until it stops.
steps.instruction: Find the shutoff valve under the sink feeding the leaking line. Turn the handle clockwise (righty-tighty) until it stops. Quarter-turn valves: turn the handle so it is perpendicular to the pipe.
steps.why: Working on a pressurised fitting sprays water and can strip threads.
success_criteria: Valve handle turned fully clockwise or perpendicular to the pipe
common_mistakes: Turning the hot valve when the cold line leaks
tips: Old valves can be stiff; use steady pressure, not a wrench on the handle
steps.narration: First thing, shut the water off right here at the valve.

steps.title: Relieve pressure
steps.tooltip: Open the faucet to drain remaining pressure.
steps.instruction: Open the faucet above. A short trickle that stops confirms the valve is closed.
success_criteria: Water flow stops within a few seconds

steps.title: Catch drips
steps.tooltip: Put a bucket or towel under the fitting.
steps.instruction: Place a bucket or folded towel directly under the valve and supply nut.
success_criteria: Bucket or towel visible under the valve

steps.title: Snug the nut
steps.tooltip: Tighten the compression nut 1/4 turn with the wrench.
steps.instruction: Hold the valve body steady with one hand. Fit the wrench on the compression nut and tighten clockwise about a quarter turn. Do not crank it.
steps.why: Compression fittings seal by squeezing a brass ferrule; a small turn usually reseats it.
success_criteria: Wrench on the nut on the valve outlet
common_mistakes: Tightening the valve packing nut instead
warnings: Stop after a quarter turn; more can crack the ferrule
steps.narration: Just a quarter turn, that's usually all it needs.

steps.title: Test
steps.tooltip: Turn the valve back on slowly and check for drips.
steps.instruction: Open the shutoff valve counter-clockwise slowly. Close the faucet. Wipe the fitting dry and watch it for a minute. If it still drips, repeat step 4 with another 1/8 turn.

faq.a: Clockwise. On quarter-turn valves, handle across the pipe means closed.
The ferrule may be damaged; the supply line or ferrule needs replacing.
